summary:
SPACE LEGENDS
Their missions ended. Their discoveries live forever.

Space Legends is an educational adventure game that introduces school-age learners and casual space enthusiasts to the machines behind historic space exploration. Guided by Nova the Astronaut and Beep-Bop the Robot, players explore artifacts across the Moon, Mars, and deep space through storytelling, interactive maps, and mission profiles.

The experience features 14 machines, including Apollo’s Eagle descent stage, Lunar Roving Vehicles, and ALSEP science stations; Mars explorers such as Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Viking, Phoenix, InSight, and Ingenuity; and deep-space missions including Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, Kepler, and Pioneer 10 and 11. Profiles explain each machine’s purpose, mission, scientific contributions, and current status.

Three mini-games—Who Am I?, Mission Memory, and Science Detective—make learning interactive. An Explorer Journal, badges, and a Space Guidebook encourage players to keep exploring.

Mission details are cross-referenced with NASA’s Space Science Data Coordinated Archive. Space Legends is an independent student project inspired by the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It is not an official NASA website and is not endorsed by NASA.
details:
Space Legends is an educational adventure game that helps school-age learners and casual space enthusiasts discover the machines left behind by historic missions. Guided by Nova the Astronaut and Beep-Bop the Robot, players explore interactive maps and artifact profiles covering 14 missions and machines across the Moon, Mars, and deep space. The profiles explain each machine’s purpose, mission, scientific contributions, location, and current status, including the distinction between surface artifacts, inactive orbiters, and probes still traveling through space.

Players can reinforce what they learn through three mini-games: Who Am I?, a mission timeline challenge, and Science Detective, which connects scientific instruments to their discoveries. An Explorer Journal, badges, a guidebook, and NASA archive links support continued learning.

The project aims to make space history approachable and memorable, helping learners see how engineering enabled scientific discovery and how past missions paved the way for later exploration. Its storytelling approach gives historic hardware a distinct voice while keeping mission facts tied to NASA’s Space Science Data Coordinated Archive.

The team created original cartoon characters and artwork and built the website using React. The project combines interactive maps, game mechanics, and beginner-friendly narratives in a format designed to invite exploration. In developing it, the team considered audience age, accessibility, factual accuracy, clear explanations, and the need to distinguish artifacts by their actual location and operational status.

Space Legends is an independent educational student project inspired by the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It is not an official NASA website and is not endorsed by NASA.
